### Running jobs

The cluster uses SLURM. The generic CPU wrapper requests a 48-core NUMA fraction on `preempt_cpu`. Packing parallelizes over cell blocks.
The training wrapper requests one GPU and 16 host cores on `preempt`, binds the workspace into the container, and invokes Python with the contents of `CMD`.
Jobs can be preempted. The training wrapper uses the work-log preemption helper and resumable checkpoints.
A restarted job can receive a new SLURM ID, so check that the final encoder file exists before using it in a dependent run. [CPU wrapper](scripts/cpu_job.sbatch) · [Packing job](scripts/pack.sbatch) · [GPU wrapper](scripts/gpu_job.sbatch) · [N078 resubmissions](.agent-research/results/N078-in-domain-ssl-scaling-sigreg-lf-pretrain/jobs.txt)

The project uses GPUs when the task is at least twice as fast as a well-parallelized CPU run. Estimate the total GPU-hours before submitting a training sweep. A sweep above 25 GPU-hours needs project approval.
Record each training submission in its experiment item, including config, job ID, budget and log path, and register its offline Weights & Biases run and sync lineage.
Compute nodes have no internet. The login-node cron syncs offline metrics. Completed runs also leave local results and predictions. [Project context](.agent-research/results/N088-literature-review-user-11-24-label-free/context.md) · [Sync script](scripts/wandb_sync_cron.sh)

## Experiment history

The links lead to the original item for each decision or result. Early scores use the label version and split in force at the time. Scores are rounded to three decimals except where extra precision identifies a record, re-base or small effect.
“Flat” refers to an item's registered comparison. A positive result for the GS student or MM3 can coexist with a flat GOAL result.
The index records completed work through N084 and N086, with N085, N087 and N088 still open in the 24 November 2026 snapshot.
The index jumps from N068 to N073. [Archive](.agent-research/notebook/INDEX_ARCHIVE.md) · [Current index](.agent-research/notebook/INDEX.md)

### Establish the dataset and the two measurable links

**[N001] · Pack and verify the release.** Converted the 50 checksum-verified Dryad chunks into indexed memory-mapped arrays for 412,941 cells.
Independent decoding found zero mismatched arrays in the sampled records. The pack became the common input format.

**[N002] · Literature review, learning through a shared modality.** Reviewed six strands of work on partial pairings, transfer and evaluation.
The review proposed hiding known pairs in a simulation to test transitive error estimates. The two real paired datasets alone could not establish GS marker accuracy. [Review synthesis](.agent-research/results/N002-literature-review-trimodal-alignment-wit/SYNTHESIS.md)

**[N003] · Audit the LF–GS matches.** Areas measured independently from matched Wright and LF phase images had Spearman correlation .740 versus .000 after shuffling.
Pairing was informative but imperfect. The outlier analysis gave a rough upper estimate around 7% for mismatches and heavy-tailed residuals together.

**[N004] · Change the project design after auditing the pairing.** All 15,712 GS cells belonged to antibody-unstained slides.
With zero GS–marker pairs, use LF as the bridge and distinguish measured same-cell endpoints from inferred marker agreement.

**[N005] · Build masked targets and calibrate the images.** Constructed 13 outputs with masks, draw-specific controls and gated cell classes.
Flat-field correction reduced brightfield background–radius correlation from −.435 to −.040. Preserve illumination direction during augmentation.

### First LF models and the spatial confound

**[N006] · Supervised ResNet-18 baseline.** On v3, mean r over 12 marker targets was .707 on held-out FOVs and .494/.471 across draws.
A three-class mean predictor matched or beat the network on several gated pooled targets. Cell type explained much of the initial signal.

**[N007] · Self-supervised pretraining.** Tested two views of a cell with disjoint illumination channels against augmentation-only views.
Frozen augmentation-only probes reached .486/.472 across draws versus .460/.435 for disjoint illumination. The stronger SSL recipe went forward to fine-tuning.

**[N008] · Test an external cell-type anchor.** A PBC classifier with .988 in-domain accuracy called 72–75% of the BSCCM Wright cells platelets.
In-domain GS clusters agreed with LF-predicted broad classes on .858 of cells. The PBC classifier did not transfer directly.

**[N009] · Bind frozen GS and marker encoders to LF.** The first fused model retrieved the exact LF cell among ten candidates only .011 of the time on the held-out GS slide.
Simpler linear contrastive alignment reached .349 within a slide and .033 across slides. Early raw-autofluorescence comparisons were revisited after N012.

**[N010] · Train the Giemsa image encoder.** Fine-tuning the last four DinoBloom blocks with stain augmentation, normalization or adversarial training yielded raw-autofluorescence r .284–.308 on the first held-out slide.
On later detrended targets the student reached .648/.323 across slides versus its LF teacher's .559/.305.

**[N011] · Diagnose slide shift.** A classifier identified the slide with .920 accuracy from GS features and .990 from LF features.
Direct GS regression on raw autofluorescence fell from about .620 within slide to .440–.450 across slides, prompting a spatial control.

**[N012] · Test position alone.** A region-blocked position model predicted raw autofluorescence and CD19 with median r .840 each.
It also predicted CD56 (.530) and CD123 (.490). Spatial backgrounds confounded several apparent biological signals.

**[N013] · Detrend the labels, v4.** Removed each slide's position trend from the targets and flagged 567 suspect image pairs.
ResNet-18 reached .555 across draws on the 12-target metric. The FOV-to-draw gap shrank from about .220 to .080.

**[N014] · Fine-tune the SSL encoder as a marker teacher.** On v4 the pretrained ResNet-50 reached .574 versus .565 for ResNet-50 trained from scratch.
Adversarial draw invariance gave .554 for the ResNet-18 arm. Fine-tuning recovered value that the frozen probes missed.

**[N015] · Pass the improved teacher to the GS student.** The student distilled from the stronger LF marker model scored .641/.303 on detrended autofluorescence across the two slides.
Improving the LF marker task gave no corresponding improvement on the GS autofluorescence endpoint.

**[N016] · Test the bridge where ground truth is available.** Split LF illumination channels into two artificial modalities and hid the direct pairs.
Error bounds covered 95% of comparisons. Distilled r .457–.488 was close to the direct oracle .465 in this same-instrument simulation.

**[N017] · Estimate GS marker error on real cells.** Combined student–teacher correlation and teacher–measurement correlation under a calibrated-teacher and conditional-independence assumption.
For draw 0 → 1 this estimated CD16 at .800 and CD123 at .170. The measured GS autofluorescence check was .649. Only the latter has same-cell truth.

**[N018] · Map information to illumination patterns.** On held-out FOVs, brightfield alone gave .585 across 12 targets, all darkfield .619 and the full stack .635.
**[N023] · Repair a pooled assay and re-base on v5.** Draw-1 pooled CD123/HLA-DR/CD14 failed dye and cell-type controls. Dropping it and changing normalization took frozen predictions from .574 to .6343.
Training on repaired labels then gave .640 against a matched .6346. Only the latter comparison measures training progress.

**[N024] · Trace the v5 labels through the GS chain.** Within-slide GS autofluorescence rose from .383/.689 to .510/.867.
MLL23 fine-contrast AUROC fell from .622 to .536. The same-cell proxy and external clinical ranking favored different teachers.

**[N025] · Use separate teachers for different readouts.** TT6 used a v4 marker teacher and a v6 autofluorescence teacher trained with unstained-slide autofluorescence.
GS autofluorescence was .578/.855 and MLL23 AUROC .611 versus the v4 chain's .622. Clinical non-inferiority remained unresolved, and review identified a target-calibration leak.

**[N026] · Model the cell at two scales.** Averaging a full-view and 2× zoomed ResNet reached .651/.652 on v5 using SSL that included unlabelled images of both draws.
A same-scale full-view ensemble gave .6438. Re-estimating batch-normalization statistics on the test draw reduced r by .005–.011.

**[N027] · Increase Giemsa-student capacity.** More trainable blocks and more steps reduced MLL23 fine-contrast AUROC from .611 to .529 with DinoBloom-B and .420 with DinoBloom-L.
Additional capacity failed to improve same-cell truth or clinical transfer.

**[N032] · Vary the LF teacher across training runs.** Four teacher runs yielded MLL23 fine-contrast means from .477 to .611.
Immature-granulocyte/myelocyte CD16 and hairy-cell HLA-DR transferred more reliably than eosinophil CD16. Subsequent clinical comparisons paired or averaged teachers.

**[N033] · Use virtual stains as labelled training data.** Generated Wright-like images for 317,935 marker-labelled cells and supplied their measured markers to the GS student.
MLL23 AUROC moved from .551 to .565, inside teacher-run variability. Extra synthetic images gave no established transfer gain.

### Generate fluorescence images and investigate the v5 plateau

**[N034] · Learn a fluorescence-image distribution and hide cell pairs.** Conditional flow matching samples possible images given LF. On the development direction it improved CRPS (a probabilistic error score, .570 vs .780 for regression) but reduced mean per-cell r to about .550 from .610.
In a separate scalar experiment with hidden pairings, bags of 16 of the same cells retained .503 versus paired .561. Different-cell bags yielded little signal.

**[N035] · Freeze the sampler and reverse the draw direction.** With 48 Heun steps and guidance 2, flow improved CRPS (.674 vs .815) and conditional Wasserstein distance (.692 vs .727), both lower-is-better metrics.
Per-cell r fell to .476 versus regression's .576. Better distributional predictions did not yield more accurate values for an individual cell.

**[N036] · Cross-fit the position correction.** Fit each spatial trend on other FOV folds and retain it only if it improves held-out variance.
The split-dependent FOV variance-share gap shrank from .055 to .017. N037 tested whether this preprocessing repair improved prediction.

**[N037] · Retrain on cross-fitted labels.** Fine-tuned the two inductive ResNets on v5cx and scored on frozen v5.
The resulting .654 versus .6527 was flat relative to seed noise.

**[N038] · Review 1, locate the v5 plateau.** Centering within FOVs raised the same N031 predictions from .6527 to .7211.
FOV-level background in the dim dye channel explained part of the gap. The review commissioned alternative labels, a label-count curve and input diagnostics.

**[N039] · Change the fluorescence background estimator.** Per-cell subtraction removed much of the FOV structure, but v8 failed the pre-registered label QC, including the draw-1 CD19 positive-mode check.
A v5 single model seeing both draws scored .678 on the GOAL cells, or .659 under data matching. V8 was set aside.

**[N040] · Complete missing labels with a noisy student.** Training against a teacher's predictions for missing entries raised single-model r from .643 to .6529.
The v5 student ensemble gave .656 versus .6527, a +.0037 gain below the registered bar despite wins in 16 of 22 target–direction pairs.

**[N041] · Randomize acquisition nuisances.** Varied LED gains, offsets, shot noise and blur with a consistency loss.
The single base model gained .0025, and the ensemble gained .0004 on v5. The augmentation gave no GOAL improvement.

**[N042] · Test whether high-frequency details limit the weak markers.** Blurring with a 1.5-pixel scale changed their correlations by at most .011.
Overall r was .641 versus .643 unblurred. The planned architecture with separate optical stems stopped at this screening test.

**[N043] · Produce the first paper figure set.** Six figures documented architecture, cross-draw markers, label limits, GS transfer, fluorescence generation and set matching.
This was a writing deliverable. The later N086 overview uses a separate figure sequence.

**[N044] · Generate residual fluorescence around a regressor.** The flow learned deviations from a predicted image mean. New-draw per-cell r rose from .550 for plain flow to .594, close to regression's .599.
CRPS was .591 versus plain flow's .569. It met the per-cell criterion and missed the calibration criteria.

**[N045] · Add semi-supervised optimal transport to paired alignment.** SOTAlign used unpaired LF and clinical smear cells in addition to the GS–LF pairs.
Across slides, mean R@10 was .028 versus .030 for paired SigLIP. Autofluorescence transfer was about .330 versus .660 for output distillation. The added alignment gave no advantage.

**[N046] · Repeat noisy-student training.** Replaced the original teacher with the N040 student ensemble and repeated label completion.
Round two scored .655 versus .656 in round one. The earlier gain did not compound.

### Re-base on v10, compare encoders and align the three modalities

**[N051] · Select a cofactor for each marker and adopt v10.** The frozen N031 ensemble moved from .6527 to .6703 on the new labels.
Scored on v10, N048 reached .6804 versus .679 for the pair trained directly on v10. The project adopted the new yardstick and subsequently set the .700 target.

**[N052] · Register the three-modality comparison.** Proposed two paired latent spaces (LF–marker and LF–GS) joined by flow, alongside a single LF hub and an output-distilled baseline.
The decision commissioned encoder tests and marker-completion tests. It produced a design, without a new performance estimate.

**[N053] · Compare pretrained encoders and combine complementary members.** The best standalone Cytoland seed scored .667 versus the v10 ResNet control's .6730. The single-encoder criterion failed.
Adding Cytoland to the N048 full/zoom pair reached .6862, then .6864 with fresh Cytoland training. This replicated ensemble gain set the official record.

**[N054] · Test the two-space model against distillation.** Cross-slide autofluorescence r was .658 for output distillation, .650 for the LF hub and .642/.625 for the two flow paths.
The unpaired final alignment gave .322. Paired latent designs carried signal, while conditional marker completion showed little transferable gain across draws.

**[N055] · Add more Cytoland variants.** The planned four-member combination used a second Cytoland scale and scored .6902.
The comparison stayed below .6916. Later variants explored label and view diversity without establishing a new record.

**[N056] · Compare anchored students and unpaired clinical adaptation.** Hub versus output distillation gave MLL23 AUROC .704 versus .568.
This comparison had unequal anchor gradient shares and missed its registered seed-range rule. Unbalanced transport, mean shift and covariance matching gave no consistent improvement.

**[N057] · Vary the class-anchor strength alone.** Raising its weight from 0.5 to 2 and 8 gave the output student MLL23 means of .568, .604 and .627.
The trend stayed within the specified seed floor, motivating a matched-strength test of the distillation target.

**[N058] · Confirm the hub under matched anchoring.** Across three LF teachers, mean MLL23 AUROC over 12 fine plus three lineage contrasts was .681 for latent distillation and .568 for output distillation.
The gain .113 exceeded the pre-specified .074 seed floor. The paired teacher test gave p = .07.

**[N059] · Review 3, separate model diversity from draw-specific readout.** The .6862 ensemble equalled an in-distribution single-model reference, while within-FOV scoring reached .726.
A few-shot readout reached .704 using labelled new-draw cells, a different protocol. The review led to head and loss experiments. Subsequent controls found no identifiable numeric ceiling.

### Output heads, label errors and training-time supervision
The three pooled targets gained about .015–.031 at a cost to singles. This trade-off suggested using different heads for the two assay types.

**[N063] · Combine the specialized heads on fresh seeds.** Take pooled outputs from the panel model and singles from the two-part model with FOV offsets. The two-part network alone scored .677 (.6766 before rounding).
The composite scored .6784 versus fresh controls .668, passing its primary comparison. Adding it to N053 gave .690, below the ensemble bar.

**[N064] · Estimate which parts of the fluorescence measurement are reliable.** Splitting pixels into checkerboard halves gave a reliability-derived r limit of .9999.
Changing the background model gave much lower agreement, particularly on CD19. The pixel check cannot establish a ceiling for predicting the complete label.

**[N065] · Rebuild the ensemble with composite heads.** The pre-specified three-composite ensemble scored .690 versus the .6916 bar.
The planned six-way *descriptive secondary* reached .6929. Only the primary comparison could advance the record.

**[N066] · Review 4, locate the directional gap.** For the frozen six-way model, draw 1 → 0 scored .704 and 0 → 1 scored .6822.
On two pooled-panel slides of the latter test draw, CD45 scored .881 and .578. Background estimators disagreed systematically by FOV, with no independent reference to decide which one was correct.

**[N067] · Train on the average of two background estimators.** The consensus-label model scored .662 against frozen v10 versus the .671 control.
CD56 fell from .504 to .444. Training on the consensus worsened the primary readout.

**[N068] · Reflect images together with the illumination channels.** Applied an anti-diagonal reflection, swapped corresponding directional LEDs and dropped the unpaired LED119.
The symmetry arm scored .669 and dropping LED119 alone gave .6718. The planned use of the exact optical symmetry was flat.

**N069 · Record unavailable.** The indexes and item directory contain no N069 experiment, score or verdict.

**N070 · Record unavailable.** The indexes and item directory contain no N070 experiment, score or verdict.

**N072 · Record unavailable.** The indexed history resumes at N073. No separate experiment or result is documented for N072. [Index](.agent-research/notebook/INDEX.md)

**[N073] · Treat clipped intensities as upper bounds.** Trained with a censored-label loss and a longer, 20-epoch schedule.
The model scored .666, down .0048 against the control. The combined recipe was flat by the project rule.

**[N074] · Predict the fluorescence image during training.** A training-only decoder received supervision from the six-channel fluorescence crop, while the LF marker head kept its original task.
The image decoder learned, but GOAL was .668 versus .671 for the control. Dense supervision failed to improve the scalar predictions.

**[N075] · Keep alternative label definitions in separate heads.** Trained a v10 head and a local-background head on the same encoder, then evaluated the v10 output.
GOAL was .671 versus .6706. Separating the targets avoided the large consensus-label loss without a detectable gain.

### Joint decoding, external donors and the current runs

**[N076] · End training on pooled-panel cells only.** Continued trained networks at low learning rate on the source draw's “all” slides.
MM3 changed by −.0012 and GOAL by −.0025. Concentrating the final updates on pooled cells was flat.

**[N077] · Review external datasets for joint-marker supervision.** Identified S-BIAD452, with nine markers measured on every cell and five overlapping BSCCM singles.
The scout led to an external donor-held-out benchmark and a shared-trunk transfer test.

**[N078] · Scale in-domain SSL.** Extending ResNet-50 pretraining to 160 epochs gave .6707. A ConvNeXt-S pretrained for 60 epochs gave .669 in the initial GOAL screen.
ConvNeXt-S improved the secondary MM3 score to .774 versus .756 for its matched ResNet seed. N083 tested replication.

**[N079] · Review 5, ask what the pooled-panel metric can establish.** On the reviewed b01 cells, a type-only predictor gave .730 versus .737 for composed single outputs and .746 for the pooled head.
That small gap exposed the limits of MM3 as evidence for within-type co-expression. The review also identified the training-step confound in the earlier label-count curve.

**[N080] · Measure joint decoding with complete truth.** Cycled train/validation/test through three ImageStream donors. Mean r was .596 with all nine labels, .526 with one random label and .542 when 10% of cells contributed pooled labels.
The within-type full-minus-single gap was .020. Whole-donor 36-pair correlation error was .189/.229/.237. The sparse regime largely missed CD4/CD8 exclusivity within T cells.

**[N081] · Train on BSCCM and ImageStream together.** Joined dataset-specific image stems to a shared trunk and overlapping marker heads.
BSCCM GOAL fell from .673 to .6673. A shared name for a marker did not make its readout interchangeable between instruments.

**[N082] · Hold optimization steps fixed in a label-count experiment.** Half the labels at 10 and 20 epochs gave .646 and .658. Full labels at 10 epochs gave .673.
At matched steps the label gain was .016, versus .012 from additional updates on the half set. Label quantity dominated this one-seed comparison.

**[N083] · Replicate the ConvNeXt-S pooled-panel gain.** The two matched MM3 gains were .0172 and .0098. Their mean gain of .0135 cleared the registered .007 threshold.
Longer SSL on the smaller draw improved its GOAL direction. Selecting 60/120 epochs by direction gave .675 for one model and .6907 when added to N053, both secondary results.

**[N084] · Confirm the fourth member.** The registered comparison added seed-1 ConvNeXt-S to the three N053 members.
GOAL was .6911, missing .6916 by .0005, with MM3 .7764. The fourth member helped reproducibly but did not advance the official GOAL record.

**[N085] · Running, combine stronger encoders and specialized heads.** Registered a union of eight equal-weight members, including 120-epoch ConvNeXt-S and composite heads, with success defined as GOAL above .6916.
The item has a plan and submitted work. Its primary result was still pending at this snapshot.

**[N086] · Publish the overview figures.** Five initial figures summarized progress, experiments, errors, joint decoding and GS transfer.
The extension added four architecture and alignment figures. The nine reviewed figures and their data sources are linked below.

**[N087] · Open, test decoders, autoencoders and flow.** Two feature-export jobs were logged. The first control is to recover the frozen ResNet head's .6730.
Experiments on low-dimensional image and marker representations, co-expression and GS matching are specified below. No final decoder comparison is recorded.

**[N088] · Open literature review.** The review covers LF prediction, low-dimensional image features, sparse multi-target decoding and image–molecular alignment.
The intended outcome is a shortlist of new, testable comparisons. No new measured GOAL or clinical result is recorded. [Review context](.agent-research/results/N088-literature-review-user-11-24-label-free/context.md)

The overview figures have downloadable PNGs, SVGs and JSON sidecars. The full captions define the comparison unit for each panel.
Where shown, whiskers are one standard deviation and rings are individual seeds, slides, teachers, donors or contrasts. A registered effect-size rule and a significance test can give different verdicts at small sample sizes. [Panel captions and statistical conventions](figures/overview/CAPTIONS.md)

Read each step within its label era. The change from v5 to v10 moves frozen models as well as new ones.

Heads, losses, label definitions, encoders and external data are compared against seed-matched ResNet controls.

### Figure 3 · Where the remaining error sits

The weak markers, the smaller training draw, the step-matched learning curve and agreement between label estimators locate different sources of error.

![Marker and direction breakdown, learning curve and label agreement](figures/overview/fig3_gap.png)

### Figure 4 · Joint decoding on two instruments

BSCCM tests pooled fluorescence. ImageStream reveals the effects of sparse supervision on all nine markers and their within-cell relationships.

![Pooled-panel accuracy on BSCCM and donor-held-out joint-marker results on ImageStream](figures/overview/fig4_multimarker.png)

### Figure 5 · Teach a Giemsa reader through LF

Clinical AUROC and measured same-cell autofluorescence compare output distillation, latent distillation, class anchoring and two-space alignment.

![Giemsa student comparison by teacher target, anchor strength and latent design](figures/overview/fig5_giemsa.png)

### Figure 6 · Follow a cell through the four-member ensemble

The input stack feeds four image encoders. Pooled features pass to sparse-supervision heads, and the marker predictions are averaged at inference.

![N084 model architecture with illumination stack, four encoders and masked training targets](figures/overview/fig6_architecture.png)

### Figure 7 · Compare encoders and build the ensemble

Strong standalone performance and complementary errors are different properties. The cf150 ResNet pair gained most from Cytoland as its third member.

![Single-encoder scores and the sequence of prediction ensembles](figures/overview/fig7_architectures.png)

### Figure 8 · Align modalities across slides

## Current work and open questions

**Can the ensemble clear .6916 on the frozen v10 protocol?** N085 combines 120-epoch source-only ConvNeXt-S pretraining on both draws with panel heads for pooled targets and two-part/FOV-offset heads for singles.
Its primary comparison is the pre-specified eight-member average. MM3, the six-member subset and standalone members are secondary. The item records the work as running. [N085] · [Registered scorer](.agent-research/results/N085-stronger-members-convnext-s-with-120-ep/n085_score.py)

**Can the decoder recover more from a fixed image?** N087 starts with the same ResNet features and compares the original head, ridge regression, reduced-rank readouts, a multilayer perceptron and nearest neighbours.
A recovered baseline of .6730 checks that the feature export and scoring agree with the original model. The proposed nonlinear follow-up requires gains above .0054 in both directions. [N087]

**What survives compression?** The image autoencoder arm trains on the source draw with latent sizes 16, 64 and 256. Held-out performance is measured by GOAL, clustering agreement with gated classes, and nearest-neighbour balanced accuracy.
PCA-compressed SSL features provide a matched-dimension control. Other arms retain the pretrained SSL projector or add a narrow bottleneck during fine-tuning. [N087]

**Can a model learn realistic marker combinations for an ambiguous image?** A marker autoencoder or PCA learns a prior on complete profiles from a separate donor.
The sandbox asks whether this reduces 36-pair error to .210 or less with at most .010 loss in macro r. A conditional flow arm samples a whole nine-marker vector from an image embedding.
It compares predicted pair correlations, CD4/CD8 exclusivity and population fractions against a mean-squared-error decoder on identical features. A follow-up with sparse labels depends on the jointly labelled test. [N087]

**Can a class-conditional match help Giemsa cells?** N087 also proposes class means and within-class optimal transport from GS embeddings to marker profiles.
Teacher agreement, measured autofluorescence and clinical contrasts remain the available endpoints. Direct GS–marker accuracy still requires a paired reference. [N087] · [Pairing audit][N004]

**Which comparisons are genuinely new?** N088 reviews LF-to-marker prediction, learned projections and autoencoders, sparse multi-target supervision, marker priors and cross-modal alignment.
The idea backlog includes a zoomed ConvNeXt-S member, ImageStream pretraining with separate downstream heads, and testing bag-level learning on cohorts with varying cell composition.
A proposal for the supervising lab is to acquire marker and Wright images on the same cells. Those pairs could test the GS bridge directly and help adjudicate proxy-label disagreement. These are proposals, with outcomes still to be measured. [N088] · [Open ideas](.agent-research/notebook/IDEAS.md)

# Agent orchestration — who reads what, when

## Context is the scarce resource
The main agent's context is the only thing surviving a whole task. Anything entering it that
the next decision does not need is waste; subagents keep large reads OUT. Parallel agents are
OPTIONAL help — use them where independent work exists and they run reliably, never as a quota.

## Read order, any non-trivial task
1. `bin/state.sh` — RULES, last 10 INDEX rows, KNOWLEDGE headline, open TODOs. Always,
   <=25 lines.
2. Only if a row/bullet is relevant: grep that item file or results folder. Never the
   whole notebook. One flat level: INDEX/KNOWLEDGE -> one detail file.
3. Project code: only the files the task touches.
Never re-read what an earlier turn established. The notebook is the memory; re-deriving is
the failure it exists to prevent.

## When to delegate
When the ANSWER is small but the READING is large: sweeping files, scanning logs, surveying
a library, checking a claim across a codebase — OR when the work is independent of what you
are doing now. Not what you can do in two tool calls, and never the judgment itself —
a subagent proposes, the main agent decides.

## Several problems at a time
Do not work one problem per attempt. When the diagnosis shows several separable problems, address them
together: bundle the changes in one attempt (baseline = the current best; ablate only what wins) or run
separate items side by side when the cluster allows. There is no one-variable rule. Reliability rules
that stay (observed failures):
- **Subagents do not own long jobs.** A Bash call tops out at 10 minutes, so a subagent that backgrounds a
  GPU job and returns delivers nothing (2026-10-07: a diagnostic agent "stopped once more on its own
  background GPU work"). For a job > ~10 min the subagent returns a ready-to-submit package; the
  coordinator submits and owns the `wait-job.sh` waiter.
- **Blocked on the user (>25 GPU-h yes, a decision) blocks that item, not the session:** ask in chat, keep
  the other work going.
- **Ending a turn** only when every pending job/agent has a harness-tracked waiter (re-arm one lost in a
  session restart) — otherwise the user has to type "go on".

## While a job runs: no idling
Any long-running work (training run, build, download, agent task) is the moment to widen the search, not to wait. Typical order (do what pays, skip the rest):
1. Read the run's early signals against the stated expectation (cheap; do not touch the job).
2. Ideate: 3-5 NEW angles on the goal — different mechanisms, data, representations, decompositions, framings — not tweaks of the
   running job. Wild or contrarian ideas are explicitly welcome. One line each in `notebook/IDEAS.md`
   (`idea · mechanism · cheapest test · status open|testing|promising|dead(why)`).
3. Agents: literature on the open question, a Codex idea-writer, an outsider or assumption-breaker (the `work-review` step-3
   briefs, lighter). Reports into the item's `agents/` folder.
4. Test the best ideas as far as cheap means allow before any real investment: CPU analyses, ceiling/oracle tests, tiny prototypes,
   cached features, offline evaluation of existing checkpoints, small GPU jobs inside the budget rules (>25 GPU-h still needs a yes;
   GPU only if >=2x a CPU run). Do not compete with the running job for its GPUs.
5. Prepare the next package (pre-registration, scripts, evaluation) so nothing waits when the run ends.
6. Record: promising -> `new-item.sh exp "<title>" module|paradigm`; dead -> IDEAS.md with the reason (and KNOWLEDGE `## Refuted` if it kills a belief).
Quality over quantity: an idea that is only a hyper-parameter of the running job does not count. The stall gate still applies to new
exp items. Ending a turn with a run going is fine once this is done (or there is nothing useful left — say so in the last message).

## The five roles (each names WHO runs it)
Order: reader -> writer -> control ‖ cross-review -> (integrator, when Codex supplied code).
Both reviewers also apply retroactively. Keep the source READ-ONLY.
- **reader** — Claude, read-only. Studies the source, writes an in-depth implementation
  spec, cites paths, <=2k tokens. Never edits.
- **writer** — **Claude OR Codex**. Implements from that spec. Default to Codex for
  large/bulk/high-context jobs — ports, multi-file changes, long reads — because keeping
  that reading entirely out of Claude's context is the real token-efficiency win: Codex
  runs as a separate process and only a <=2k-token handback re-enters Claude's context,
  which is cheaper than even a Claude subagent. Keep small, quick, single-file edits with
- Push the working branch after every commit and before the session ends; a repo without a remote gets one (private GitHub under Jetzu) or a vault git bundle (`/home/vault/v181bb/v181bb10/git_bundles/`) before any further work. Unpushed = unsaved (user ruling 2026-11-07).
  Claude directly — dispatching, gating (`codex-check.sh`) and integrating a Codex job costs
  more turns than writing three lines. Codex writes only into `results/N###-slug/codex/`,
  never the live tree, regardless of which hat it's wearing.
- **control** — **Claude Opus**, or a script where mechanizable. Reads BOTH implementations
  and checks equivalence, plus equivariance for geometric models; or re-derives the key
  number by a DIFFERENT route. Catches the confident-wrong answer. Its independence comes
  from the METHOD, not the model — so same-family is right, a script is better, and
  spending Codex here buys almost nothing. Unaffected by who wrote the code.
- **cross-review (red-team)** — **whichever model did NOT write it.** Claude writes ->
  Codex red-teams (`/codex:rescue`). Codex writes -> Claude red-teams (`/code-review` or a
  general-purpose subagent, same adversarial brief). Attacks the conclusion: the confound,
  the tautology, the leak, the trivial baseline that would score the same. Its independence
  comes from PRIORS, the one thing another model family supplies — a same-family reviewer
  regenerates the confounds its own family already considered. Mandatory, not scoped to
  high-stakes jobs: anything acted on or marked `[verified]` gets cross-reviewed by the
  other model, every time.
- **integrator** — Claude. Checks Codex's code in `results/N###-slug/codex/` against the
  real tree, adapts it to local interfaces and conventions, lands it. The only agent that
  lands Codex code. Never copy blindly: a fix built outside the tree misses local context.
Pair reader+writer per job. Add control and cross-review to anything acted on or written to
KNOWLEDGE as `[verified]`.

## Contract for every subagent
State explicitly: (a) the ONE question or change, (b) its results path
`.agent-research/results/N###-slug/`, (c) "write outputs only there, return <=2k tokens,
cite every number with a path or command", (d) what NOT to touch, (e) if it waits on a
job: one backgrounded blocking call, never a repeated check.
Parallel subagents must not write the same file. Launch independent ones in one message;
serialize anything with a dependency.

## Evidence discipline
- Every number carries its source. No source, no claim.
- A subagent's claim is `[unverified]` until a control or a file read confirms it.
- **Reviewers report; the main agent decides.** Never start a fix on a red-team, control or
  Codex finding you have not reproduced FIRST-HAND — open the cited file:line, rerun the
  cited command, build the trivial baseline it claims would score the same. Only a
  reproduced finding starts the fix. If it does not reproduce, say so in the item and leave
  the code alone: a confident reviewer is still a model, and a false positive costs more
  than the review saved. Both ways — "NOTHING BREAKS" is not proof either, just one search
  that found nothing.
- Name a baseline (the current best) and a stated expected result BEFORE the run; add a kill criterion.
  An attempt may change several things at once (no one-variable rule); ablate only what wins. A result
  without a baseline is not a result.
- Replication: screen on ONE seed against the GOAL.md bar (2 x noise). Run the >= 3-seed replication at the
  END OF EACH MAJOR ACCOMPLISHMENT (a new headline number, before it is called verified, committed or put
  in a PR) — not per candidate, not for every small step.
- Before believing a signal, name the trivial explanation that would produce it anyway
  (constant predictor, tautology, shared clock, warm start) and rule it out.
- Save every measured value (all arms/seeds/metrics/steps, long csv/json) in `results/N###-slug/`
  (>5 MB: cite the external path). 10-24: 139/350 closed exps had numbers only in prose.
- Plot every comparison (`bin/plot-compare`, one per comparison+metric) -> `plots/<metric>_<date>.png`,
  cited in the item. `effect.sh --value` refuses the label without both (void/n/a exempt).

## Waiting on long work
**The cost is the TURN, not the sleep.** A backgrounded call burns nothing and re-invokes
you when it exits; a foreground one spends the turn doing nothing. So: background it.

A PreToolUse hook (`~/.claude/hooks/no-noop-wait.sh`) blocks, in the foreground only:
a command that does nothing (`true`, `:`, filler `echo`), one *described* as a wait that
waits on nothing, one leading with `sleep` under 300s, and a loop polling `squeue`/`sacct`.
It allows anything backgrounded, a sleep used as a settle or timeout inside real work, and
heredoc bodies (writing a watcher script is authoring, not polling). Measured against 14,428
real commands from this machine's history: 3.5% blocked, all of them genuine waits. Blocked?
Background it — relabelling or swapping in a different no-op is what it exists to catch.

History: banning waits by name only relocated the spam (`Bash(true)`, `echo .`). Cheapest pattern first:
1. **Harness-tracked work** (Agent, background Bash, Workflow) — no check at all.
2. **SLURM** — be notified, don't poll. One backgrounded call prints every transition and
   the end state with elapsed + exit code:
       Bash(run_in_background=true): bin/wait-job.sh <jobid> [<jobid>...]
   Exit 0 = all COMPLETED; 1 = a FAILED/TIMEOUT/CANCELLED/OOM job, named in the output.
   Pass every job to ONE waiter, not one waiter each.
3. **Other external state** (CI, a remote queue) — ONE backgrounded blocking call.
4. **A deadline you must tick against** — `ScheduleWakeup`/`/loop`/`Monitor`: 5 min floor,
   20-30 min idle, 1200s+ when something else is the real wake signal. Double after two
   consecutive `noop` ticks — a noop reported nothing, so a longer gap loses nothing.

Name the waiter or the interval in every subagent brief that waits on a job (<=10 min foreground
only — longer jobs are the coordinator's: see 'Several problems at a time').

## Jobs: preempt by default
Helma `preempt` (GPU) / `preempt_cpu`: 1 node, 2 d max, default time 10 min (set `--time`), PreemptMode=
CANCEL (never requeued), 15 min SIGTERM->SIGKILL grace, exempt the first 2 h. Use them unless the job is
multi-node, cannot restart, or has a hard deadline (say which on submit).
- Preempt-safe = resume from latest ckpt, ckpt <=30 min (atomic tmp+rename), save+exit on SIGTERM, keep
  latest+best. Wrap: `exec bin/preempt-run.sh -- <cmd>` (`templates/preempt.sbatch`): on SIGTERM/SIGUSR1
  (`--signal=B:USR1@900`) it resubmits the saved batch script `afterany`, forwards SIGTERM, waits. Options
  in `#SBATCH` lines, parameters in env vars (the command line is not replayed). Tested 10-24 (1120092).
- Mock tests: `bin/preempt-selftest.sh`. `wait-job.sh` follows the chain (`~/.claude/state/preempt-chain/<job>.next`). Stop with
  `bin/preempt-cancel.sh` (plain scancel = SIGTERM = resubmit). wandb: glob logs by job name.
- >25 GPU-h ask: rough estimate from known step times; never a measuring job. Preempt counts too.

## Housekeeping: files and quotas (advisory, every few turns)
Quotas bite on FILE COUNT: /home/hpc ~443k soft/543k hard, /hnvme ~61k/81k (grace, then writes fail -
git, logs, ckpts for every project).
- `bin/quota.sh` (15-min cache); `--warn` prints in state.sh and, at most every 30 min per session, the prompt hook at >=90% soft.
- Big files -> `/hnvme`. Many small TEMP files -> home subdir, deleted at task end. Permanent many-file
  sets: pack (LMDB/tar/HDF5/squashfs). Envs/tools: apptainer `.sif`, no new conda/pip trees.
- Every few turns: delete own stale SLURM logs (metrics synced), wandb dirs, caches, core dumps, superseded
  ckpts, scratch/test output. Look first; own project only.

## Stall guard: 5 flat attempts -> project review
Why: Kale closed ~18 exp items (~13 real attempts) after its TM 0.544 plateau (N042) on width, depth,
seeds, encoders, contact-map refiners; TRIAD_v2 spent N022-N041 (4 HARM, 3 VOID, 1 PARTIAL, 2 thin
wins) on low-t canaries. Both were broken only when the USER typed "big ideas". The guard automates that, at
the user's own patience: a replay of both INDEX files (`evidence/2026-10-08/replay_labels.tsv`, borderline labels
flip verdicts) puts both repos at 9/10 when the user stepped in (TRIAD_v2 strict reading: 52 h earlier). Limit 10 -> 5
on 2026-10-24 (user). MUNDANE would not have fired (their work was module-scale).
- `notebook/GOAL.md` (`bin/goal.sh init`): ONE numeric end metric, target + who set it, best, `noise` = 1 sd of
  identical reruns (measured; source named), constraints. Counting starts at `--since` (default: latest item).
- ONE `exp` item per hypothesis (later jobs go into it); `new-item.sh exp "<title>" knob|module|paradigm`.
- Close an attempt: `bin/effect.sh N### improved|flat|worse --value V | --void` (n/a only `--why infra|measurement`).
  `improved` counts only if V beats `best` by > 2 x noise (the believable single-run delta); else flat.
  Unlabelled closed exp = flat; void = flat; scale `?` counts as knob. Ordered by item ID.
- `bin/stall.sh` counts flat/worse in a row since the last `improved` or closed review. At `stall_limit`:
  state.sh + the per-prompt hook print REVIEW DUE and `new-item.sh exp|task|fix|analysis` is REFUSED until a
  `review` item is open AND its `attempts.md` exists. >= 8 of the last 10 attempts knob-level (MUNDANE): knob/unscaled
  exp refused until opened as module/paradigm. A user-requested run overrides with `STALL_OVERRIDE="<their words>"` (logged).
- REVIEW DUE -> `work-review` skill, autonomous. Close with `bin/review-close.sh N###` (checks attempts/diagnosis/
  ideas/declined files, >= 4 agent reports, >= 3 scale-tagged portfolio exps incl. a paradigm one). Review #2 also tells the user plainly.
- Checked by `bin/selftest.sh` (62 cases, incl. the evidence gate: injection, N1000, races, boundaries, gating). No GOAL.md = guard off.

## Compaction survival
Whatever must outlive the session goes in the notebook, not the transcript: the decision,
its reason, the number, the path. Assume the transcript is gone.

## Two-strike loop: Codex builds in its own folder, Claude integrates
Failure rescue is one trigger for routing a job to Codex, not the only one (see below) —
but it still follows this shape. After TWO failed Claude attempts, stop retrying — two
failures mean the approach is wrong and a third try searches the same priors. Codex DOES
write code here, but never into the live tree, so a real tested implementation crosses over
instead of prose while the repo keeps exactly one writer.
1. **Codex** (`/codex:rescue`): give it the problem, ALL prior attempts and why each
   failed, the files, and its folder. It root-causes, writes and TESTS a fix in
   `results/N###-slug/codex/`, and delivers the plan — what it changed, why, what it could
   not test.
2. **integrator** (Claude): check it against the real tree, adapt, land it.
3. **Claude cross-reviews what LANDED** (`/code-review` or a general-purpose subagent, the
   same adversarial brief Codex uses on Claude's code), not what Codex proposed —
   integration is where fixes break.
4. Still broken? Next round with every prior round attached so it gives NEW ideas. When two
   rounds repeat themselves, stop: that is a stall — run `work-review` (it tells the user plainly).
Log per round: hypothesis, what was tested, and what was wrong with the APPROACH — the
durable lesson, not the diff.

## Codex scope and cadence
Codex quota is ample (2026-10-04): a regular writer AND reviewer. A job routed to Codex enters
Claude's context only as a <=2k-token handback — default it for bulk ports, multi-file work, long
reads; keep quick single-file edits with Claude (a Codex round-trip costs more turns than three
lines). Cross-review is UNCONDITIONAL: the model that did NOT write it red-teams it before it is
acted on or marked `[verified]`, any compute request over 25 GPU-h, and at the end of each two-strike round.

**A Codex job can report `completed` having run nothing.** Verified 2026-09-25: four
rescues were recorded `completed` while bwrap failed on every command
(`max_net_namespaces = 0`; fixed, but the failure mode remains). Never read the status
field as evidence — gate every result:
    bin/codex-check.sh <job-id>          # OK, or CODEX-UNAVAILABLE + exit 2
On `CODEX-UNAVAILABLE` or out-of-quota: do not retry Codex, do not skip — rerun the
red-team with a Claude subagent and write "red-team was same-family (codex unavailable)"
in the item. Weaker coverage beats a `[verified]` bullet nothing ever attacked.

## Invoking Codex
**Default: `bin/codex-run.sh <out-dir> <brief-file> [--ro] [--timeout-min N]`**, called with Bash
`run_in_background: true` (you are re-invoked on exit; no user slash command, no polling). Write the
whole prompt (hat, ONE task, contract, paths) to a brief FILE first - it goes in on stdin, so no
quoting traps. `out-dir` = `results/N###-slug/codex/` = Codex's cwd and only writable root. It
runs plain `codex exec` (no plugin broker, no Sonnet forwarder in between), gates itself, and ends
with one line: `OK ...` (exit 0) or `CODEX-UNAVAILABLE <why>` (exit 2 -> redo with Claude, never
skip). Handback = `<out-dir>/codex_last_message.md`; full stream = `codex_run.jsonl`. Gate = a
finished turn + non-empty handback + no quota/model/sandbox/sqlite failure signature (one retry,
transient infrastructure errors only). Resume a thread: `codex exec resume --last` in the same cwd.

Why not the plugin by default (found 2026-10-17): the
`codex:codex-rescue` forwarder is told "if the Bash call fails, return NOTHING" - an empty reply is
a failure, not "no findings"; it takes `cwd` from whatever it parses out of the prompt (a garbled
path was reported as "Codex CLI is not installed"); and every `task` leaves a broker + app-server
alive holding the NFS sqlite DBs - the SessionEnd hook only tears down the broker of the SESSION's
cwd, so brokers started for other workspaces are orphaned for days (one lived 10 days). Fallback if
you do use it: `/codex:rescue` via the Agent tool (`subagent_type: "codex:codex-rescue"`); treat an
empty return as CODEX-UNAVAILABLE. `/codex:transfer|status|result|cancel` are user-only; Claude can
query with `bin/codex-jobs.sh list | result <job-id> | status [--all]` and gate with `bin/codex-check.sh <job-id>`.
Wrapper `~/.local/bin/codex` now also sets `CODEX_SQLITE_HOME` to node-local `/scratch/.privtmp/<user>/codex-sqlite`
(NFS sqlite locks were the likely cause of the intermittent "failed to initialize sqlite state runtime" -
[unverified], not reproducible in 16 parallel launches).
Always name the hat: **write** (implement a spec, build+test in its folder — regular
implementation work, not just rescue), **red-team** (attack, change nothing), or **fix
round** (root-cause + build in its folder, after two Claude failures). A write job gets the
same contract as any subagent (the ONE task, its results path, what not to touch) plus the
spec or source files it needs.

**What to give a red-team — either direction.** Never "review this". Hand it the claim, the
evidence and the paths, and ask it to break the claim. This applies whether Codex is
red-teaming Claude's code or Claude (via `/code-review` or a general-purpose subagent) is
red-teaming Codex's landed code — same brief, model swapped:
  "Claim: <finding, with its number>. Evidence: <paths / commands / config>.
   Do not fix anything. Find why this claim is wrong:
   (a) what trivial baseline — constant, shuffle, copy of the input — gives this same number?
   (b) is it tautological: does a flag, override or shared schedule force what is measured?
   (c) where could the answer leak into the input?
   (d) is it measured at a flattering point — one step, seed, length, best checkpoint?

measurements on a climbing curve; a collapsed Procrustes mean scoring well; recall read as
precision) — ask them every time, regardless of which model wrote the code under review.

id, or it is not a record. A Codex/Claude disagreement is itself evidence worth logging.
# work-log protocol

## Containment (hard)
- All under `<repo>/.agent-research/` — hidden, committed. `notebook/` = index + knowledge;
  `results/N###-slug/` = that entry's outputs. Never `.claude/` or `.agents/`.
- Every figure, table, CSV, log excerpt, one-off script or report goes in that `results/`
  folder; only real project code goes elsewhere.
- Outputs >5 MB stay where produced, referenced by absolute path
  (`notebook/META.md` large_output_location).
- Exception: comparison plots → `.agent-research/plots/<metric>_<date>.png`.
- Hidden dir: ALWAYS explicit `.agent-research/` paths in Glob/Grep/scripts.

## When to log
Only work producing a commit, result, decision or non-obvious lesson, or >~10 tool calls.

## Before
`bin/new-item.sh <type> "<title>"` — exp task fix research analysis writing decision review.
Creates `notebook/items/N###-slug.md` + `results/N###-slug/` + an INDEX row (`open`).

## During
All outputs into that results folder. Experiment: a stated hypothesis with an expected result, a named baseline (the current best), a
kill criterion — before launching; an attempt may change several things at once. Screen on 1 seed
(bar = 2 x noise); >= 3-seed replication at the end of each MAJOR accomplishment. ONE `exp` item per hypothesis. A TRAINING run gets its item AT
SUBMIT (job id, config/branch, gpus x time, log path) and must be registered in wandb with
its job id in the sync lineage — compute nodes have no internet, the login cron is the only
path.
Save every measured value (long csv/json `arm,seed,metric,value[,x]`) here; plot each comparison:
`bin/plot-compare --metric M --csv F --item N### --baseline A`, cite the png (`effect.sh` checks both).
Jobs: preempt + `bin/preempt-run.sh`; GPU-h = rough estimate, no measuring jobs.

## After
1. Fill the item; update the INDEX row (status, one-line outcome, commit hash); append to
   `notebook/log.jsonl`. Closing an attempt at a goal: `bin/effect.sh N### improved|flat|worse|n/a
   [--value V] [--scale knob|module|paradigm]` (improved counts only if it beats GOAL.md best by
   more than its noise; an unlabelled closed exp counts as flat).
2. A result killing a prior belief goes to KNOWLEDGE `## Refuted` with what killed it —
   refutations are findings, never dropped.
3. Edit KNOWLEDGE only if understanding changed — single bullets, never a rewrite:
   `K###: <finding|decision|gotcha> [verified|partial|unverified] (N###; path) {cites:n}`
4. Follow-ups → `notebook/TODO.md`.
5. Every number or claim cites its source (path, command, URL). No source, no claim.

## Housekeeping (advisory)
Mind the `QUOTA` line; clean up every few turns. `.sif` envs, packed data; big → `/hnvme`, small temp → home subdir,
deleted at end; drop stale logs/caches/old ckpts. ORCHESTRATION.md 'Housekeeping'.

## Lint and review
`LINT DUE` from `state.sh`/`new-item.sh` → run `work-lint` immediately, without asking.
`REVIEW DUE` (stall guard: 5 flat attempts in a row vs `notebook/GOAL.md`; `new-item.sh` refuses
exp|task|fix|analysis) → run `work-review` at once. New goal-driven project → `bin/goal.sh init` first.
Details: ORCHESTRATION.md 'Stall guard'.

- Commit ONLY a coherent block (submodule/feature/fix) that is DONE and that control AND
  red-team passed — not mid-change. Code + its `.agent-research/` records in ONE commit,
  `N###: <summary>`; hash into the INDEX row.
- NEVER commit or push on default/main. Working branch only; push per finished block.
- PR gate: list EVERY pipeline the change touches, each with its exact command and exit

- The PR states the changes and that evidence; resolve every conflict.
- Merges into main are the USER's, by hand. Never merge, never auto-merge.

Order: reader -> writer -> control ‖ cross-review. Both reviewers also apply retroactively to
existing code. Keep the source READ-ONLY.

# N088 synthesis: three literature reviews (A label-free/representations, B sparse multi-target, C alignment/shift), 104 references
## What the literature says about our open questions
- Autoencoder latents cluster cell identity worse than SSL in every microscopy comparison (cytoself without its identity pretext 3-5x
  worse; Lu et al. 2019 AE 42.5 % vs SSL 88.0 % kNN) and small bottlenecks keep illumination/background variance (A). -> N087 AE arm is a
  test, not a hope.
- Post-projector features are worse than backbone features; SIGReg makes the projector output isotropic (no clusters by design) (A).
- Distribution alignment (DANN/OT/CORAL) provably fails when class proportions differ between domains (Zhao et al. ICML 2019) (C) ->
  explains N014/N026/N056.
- The within-slide LF<->Giemsa retrieval (.38-.40) may be a field-of-view shortcut (~3 paired cells per field) (C) -> audit.
- The only unused information channel in BSCCM training is each cell's own measured marker (B); external joint data is the only source
  of cross-marker structure (B).
- Feature-preserving fine-tuning (LP-FT, lower encoder LR, WiSE-FT) is the one lever both A and C rate highest for a 2-draw shift and
  that was never applied to our in-domain SSL encoders (Kumar et al. ICLR 2022; Wortsman et al. CVPR 2022). In-house evidence: Cytoland
  encoder LR x0.1 .6671 vs x1.0 .6464 (N053).
## Portfolio (GPU-h; status)
1. N090 gentle fine-tuning of SSL ResNet-50: encoder LR x0.1 / x0.3 (2 seeds x 2 directions, ~3 h; launched), then LP-FT + WiSE-FT
   interpolation (Codex code). Pre-registered bar +.0054 over control .6706 (2-seed mean).
2. N087 (running): decoder sweep, image AE, marker prior, flow decoder (done: no co-expression gain), equal-label-count control (B).
3. Missing-marker completion from the measured marker (B-P1): free CPU gate in the sandbox, then ~5-6 h.
4. Field-of-view shortcut audit (C-P1, CPU), then nuisance-aware LF<->Giemsa alignment (~2.5 h) only if the audit confirms it.
5. Nested (Matryoshka) projection head (A-P2, sandbox first, ~2-3 h) replaces N087-D3 (narrow backbone, predicted harmful).
6. Cell-type mixture head with S-BIAD452 profiles (B-P2, ~3 h) after the equal-label-count control.
7. DINO-style in-domain SSL (A-P3, ~6 h) and cross-slide positives in SSL (C-P3, ~4 h): diverse ensemble members.

## 0. Bottom line

1. **Autoencoder latents cluster cell identity worse than SSL or pretext-task features.** Every direct microscopy comparison found points the same way, and none goes the other way.
   - Lu 2019, yeast localisation kNN: AE **42.5 %** vs paired-cell-inpainting SSL **88.0 %** vs supervised 92.4 %.
   - cytoself ablation: a pure VQ-VAE (no identity pretext) clusters 3-5x worse (score 1.13 / 1.26 vs 3.41 / 5.96). Removing the decoder costs only ~13-25 %.
   - Ternes 2022: VAEs "often fail to identify biologically informative features due to uninformative technical variation".
   - Theory (Balestriero & LeCun, ICML 2024): reconstruction spends capacity on the top-variance pixel subspace, which is the least informative for perception.
   - A SMALLER AE bottleneck keeps only the highest-variance directions. In LED-array data those are illumination, background, size and focus. [derived] So k = 16 should be the worst of N087 C's arms.

2. **Post-projector features are worse than backbone features.**
   - SimCLR: > 10 points under linear evaluation.
   - Guillotine regularisation: up to 30 points.
   - Fine-grained / subclass information is lost after the projector: CIFAR-100 fine labels 36.0 vs 25.7 (SupCon), 33.7 vs 29.7 (supervised).
   - SIGReg pushes the projector output to an isotropic Gaussian. [derived] That space therefore has no cluster structure by construction; clusters must be read from the backbone.
   - A small projector is harmless. LeJEPA linear probe: proj. dim 64 gives 75.65 and 1024 gives 74.79.
   - A narrow backbone is not harmless: effective rank tracks downstream quality (RankMe, ICML 2023).
   - "Small from the start" in the literature means wide backbone + nested / small projection (Matryoshka: 14x smaller embedding at equal ImageNet accuracy), not a narrow encoder.

3. **Label-free marker accuracies in the literature sit at or below our numbers.** Lineage markers reach r .8-.9 with any optics. Dim lymphoid markers are .4-.6 even at 60x IFC (DeepIFC CD19 .61, CD56 .53, CD8 .41). Nothing reports cross-batch (different-draw) marker regression. No new BSCCM user was found since N066.

4. **The one untested lever the literature strongly supports for our two-draw shift is feature-preserving fine-tuning.** That means LP-FT, a lower encoder LR, and WiSE weight interpolation.
   - Literature: LP-FT ~+10 points OOD over full fine-tuning on 10 shift benchmarks.
   - The project already has a strong in-house signal. The external Cytoland encoder fine-tuned at encoder lr x1.0 scored .6464 vs .6671 at x0.1 (+.021, N053).
   - The in-domain SIGReg r50 / ConvNeXt-S encoders have only ever been fine-tuned at full LR (N078, N083: lr 5e-4, one group).

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Predictions for the running N087 arms (to check against when they land)

| N087 arm | Literature prediction | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| A rank-k / MLP / kNN on fine-tuned features | rank <= ~13 recovers the head; MLP / kNN within +.003 | C5 (nonlinearity matters for frozen reconstruction features, not task-aligned ones), K042 |
| A on frozen SSL features | MLP > ridge by a clear margin; stage 3 >= stage 4 (P4) | C5, C7, D2 |
| C image AE k = 16 / 64 / 256 | clusters worse than the SIGReg backbone; worst at k = 16; GOAL from latents far below SSL ridge | C1, C2, C3, C4 |
| D1 SSL projector outputs | 256-d output < 2048-d projector hidden layer < backbone, on clustering and markers | D1, D2, D3, D6 |
| D2 32-d bottleneck fine-tune | GOAL flat (+-.003); SSL-projector init <= fresh init; b01 not better | D7, D9, D2 |
| D3 narrow SSL from the start | worse or equal; replace by P2 (nested projection) | D4, D5, D6, D7 |

## 0. Bottom line

1. **[derived] Two kinds of joint structure; only one can move the GOAL.** Write y = f(x) + e.
   - **(i) Function-level coupling.** The f_k share structure: low rank, shared cell states.
     - This can raise per-marker r, but only if it adds information the shared trunk does not already have.
     - Bonilla et al. 2007 prove that in a noise-free block design "a cancellation of inter-task transfer occurs".
     - A shared-trunk multi-head net already implements function-level coupling. This is consistent with the flat panel-latent head
       (N062 .6704 vs .6706) and predicts a flat N087 rank-k sweep.
   - **(ii) Residual coupling, Cov(e_j, e_k | x).** Example: CD4 vs CD8 among look-alike T cells.
     - It cannot change E[y_k|x] (tower property), so it does not move per-marker Pearson.
     - It decides co-expression and gating, i.e. the user's multi-marker priority. N080 shows single-stain training loses it
       (CD4-CD8 in T: true -.81, full -.36, single -.07).
2. **The one information channel still unused is the observed marker of each training cell.**
   - Today y_j trains only head j.
   - Through a cell-state model it also says something about the cell's other markers: an observed CD3-high lymphocyte is not a B or
     NK cell. Using this creates supervision for the label-starved heads (N082: labels, not steps, limit the GOAL).
   - Partial-label literature reports large gains from exactly this:
     - Cole 2021, single positive per image: VOC 86.5 vs 86.7 mAP with full labels, linear setting.
     - Chen 2022 (SST): +5.6 mAP at 10 % known labels.
     - Li 2022 (MTPSL), one task label per image: NYUv2 segmentation 25.8 -> 30.4 (full labels 37.0); on Cityscapes it beats full
       labels.
   - Hard caveat from SST: completions must be image-specific. Dataset-level co-occurrence statistics HURT (55.3 vs 64.1 mAP at
     10 %). For us, a global residual covariance is the wrong prior; a state-conditional (mixture) prior is the right one.
3. **External joint data is the only source of the cross-marker emission structure.** BSCCM cannot identify it (K045).
   - The marker-matrix cell-typing models (CellAssign, Astir) are the template: a probabilistic cell state plus a marker-by-state
     emission matrix.
   - Here the matrix would be LEARNED from S-BIAD452, not hand-coded. Hand-coded exclusivity, as in the exclusion loss of Shi 2021,
     stays declined.
4. **Pooled channels have an exact likelihood.**
   - Gaussian closure under sums (Zhang 2020, aggregate observations) and the "marginal loss" of Shi 2021 (merged classes =
     summed probabilities) give the right observation model for a dye that carries CD3+CD19+CD56.
   - The sum is taken in linear intensity, then mapped to asinh.
   - N062's panel head was a linear-in-asinh approximation.
5. **Domain ceilings: expect small per-marker gains, real joint-coherence gains, and a risk of over-correlation.**
   - Single-cell imputation: per-protein accuracy is set by anchor/kNN methods. Seurat v4/v3 (PCA) top a 12-method benchmark (Li 2025).
   - Joint generative models (totalVI, sciPENN, CytoVI) win on uncertainty and integration, not clearly on per-protein r.
   - Imputation is cluster-level: Mocking 2023 F 0.53-0.87, "limited similarity at the cell level".
   - A marker without a backbone signature is not imputable: Infinity Flow's TCR Vβ7.
   - Joint image models over-correlate marker pairs (HistoPlexer CD3:CD8a).
6. **Not proposed** (section 3, end): reduced-rank / task-covariance heads (N087-A covers them), output flows (N087-E covers them),
   label-proportion learning (set-level is known to fail here), and group-noise losses (N061 flat).

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## (ii) Diagnosis: why the cross-slide collapse happens, and what usually fixes it

### Collapse of LF<->Giemsa retrieval across slides
1. **The within-slide number is probably inflated by a shared-nuisance shortcut** [derivation, testable at zero GPU cost; see P1].
   - What the two modalities share: the LF and Wright images of one cell come from the same slide position. They share FOV-level and
     position-level nuisance: focus/z-tilt, coverslip or medium thickness, illumination fall-off, background/debris and local density.
   - Project evidence that both modalities carry position:
     - LF features predict slide position at r .92 (K007).
     - Position alone predicts autofluorescence on Giemsa cells at r .72 (N012).
     - A linear probe identifies the slide at .92 accuracy from Giemsa (DinoBloom) features and .99 from LF features (N011).
   - The arithmetic is unfavourable. The paired slides hold 10,015/5,697 cells in 2,774/1,962 FOVs, i.e. 3.6/2.9 cells per FOV (N045
     report). The within-slide validation gallery is about 279 held-out but spatially INTERLEAVED FOVs (~1,000 cells).
   - So a head that only identifies the FOV, or its slide neighbourhood, would already reach a large R@10. Chance is ~.01, and perfect
     FOV identification would give ~1.
   - Two further facts point the same way:
     - The N045 checkpoints were chosen on exactly this within-slide R@10, a selection rule that rewards the shortcut (refs 16, 22).
     - SigLIP beats CCA 2.5x within the slide (.41 vs .16) but only 1.8x across slides (.038 vs .021). The nonlinear head buys mostly
       slide-specific matching.
   - Contrastive theory predicts this outcome:
     - easy shared features suppress harder ones (31);
     - injected shared shortcuts are learned "mostly" (32);
     - site signatures dominate the distances of even large foundation models (26-28).
2. **Across slides the shortcut map is invalid.** Each slide has its own position -> nuisance field, and only one Wright-stained slide
   exists per draw. Leftover retrieval of 10-20x chance is what coarse lineage/size matching yields.
   - This matches K035/K038: the aligned space finds the same cell well above chance but carries little marker information.
   - The cross-slide number is the honest one. The within-slide number should not be used to select or compare alignment methods.
3. **Why OT/GW/SOTAlign could not repair it.**
   - GW and manifold alignment match each space's dominant geometry, which here is nuisance plus lineage (refs 9, 27-28).
   - Balanced OT mis-assigns when compositions differ (SCOTv2).
   - These methods were validated mostly with perfect correspondences (TopoGAN critique of MMD-MA/UnionCom).
   - Few-anchor OT helps only when pairs are scarce (13), and we have 15.7k.
   - The successful methods all bring outside supervision: pairs (MatchCLOT), labels (labeled GW, Yang's anchors) or targets (MolPhenix
     soft targets). In our case that is the distillation of LF outputs, which is already the best bridge.
4. **What usually fixes it.**
   - Make the shortcut useless: negatives that share the nuisance (same-FOV or same-region "ring" negatives, ref 33), spatially
     blocked validation (26), and linear erasure of known nuisance variables (LEACE, ref 33).
   - Give positives that do NOT share it: cross-batch positives (CDCL 14.3 -> 53.6 kNN, ref 25) or mutual nearest neighbours across
     batches (29).
   - Reference-based correction (TVN, sphering, Harmony, CytoNorm) works in Cell Painting only because every batch contains biologically
     identical controls (23-24). BSCCM has no such cross-draw reference, and using the held-out draw's images is transductive.

## (iii) Experiment proposals, ranked by expected value

GOAL arithmetic: 22 cells (11 targets x 2 directions), seed noise .0027, registered bar = control + .0054 (single model) or > .6916
(ensemble). Screens use 1 seed x 2 directions; a second seed only if the screen passes. Compute estimates come from the project's
measured costs (r50 GOAL fine-tune ~.7 H100-h per direction; r50 60-ep SSL ~5 H100-h per draw, N078/N085). Everything is on the
preempt queue and far below the 25 GPU-h approval line.

### P1 (rank 1). FOV/position-shortcut audit of LF<->Giemsa alignment, then nuisance-conditional alignment and distillation
- **Objective:** LF->Giemsa cross-slide transfer (secondary: honest metric for all alignment work).
- **Hypothesis:**
  - Within-slide R@10 ~.40 is mostly FOV/position identification from nuisance shared by both modalities.
  - Removing that shortcut lowers the within-slide number but raises cross-slide retrieval and the information in the bridge.
- **Recipe:**
  - Step 0 (CPU, 48 cores, ~1-2 h). Use the N045 v2 embeddings, or recompute frozen LF SSL-r50 and DinoBloom-B Giemsa features on the
    15.7k pairs. For the SigLIP-pairs and CCA heads:
    - (a) Split within-slide R@10 into FOV-hit@10 (any cell of the query's FOV in the top 10) and within-FOV R@1 (chance 1/n_FOV, about
      .28-.34).
    - (b) Position-only retrieval: cross-fit (blocked by FOV) a ridge/GBM regressor from each modality's embedding to slide (x, y),
      plus an FOV focus proxy (FOV-mean LF brightfield sharpness). Retrieve by distance between the predicted positions.
    - (c) Nuisance erasure, then refit the heads:
      - FOV-mean centring per modality: subtract each FOV's mean embedding, computed from that FOV's own images, so it is
        inductive per FOV;
      - LEACE on (x, y) polynomial features.

"""Score GOAL arms on frozen v10 labels (targets_v5cx_v10.npz), common-11, mean over b10/b01, per seed; paired deltas vs a control arm.
usage: score_goal_arms.py OUTDIR control=run_s0,run_s1 armA=run_s0,run_s1 [armB=...]
  each run name is the prefix WITHOUT the _b10/_b01 suffix; seeds are paired by position.
writes OUTDIR/goal_arms.csv (arm, seed, direction, target, r), OUTDIR/goal_summary.csv, OUTDIR/plot_goal.csv (arm,value,seed)."""
import sys, os, numpy as np, pandas as pd
W = '/hnvme/workspace/v181bb10-bsccm'; T = np.load(W + '/targets_v5cx_v10.npz', allow_pickle=True); Y, M = T['Y'], T['mask']
names = [str(n) for n in T['names']]; c11 = [j for j, n in enumerate(names[:12]) if 'CD123/HLA' not in n]
out = sys.argv[1]; arms = dict(a.split('=', 1) for a in sys.argv[2:]); arms = {k: v.split(',') for k, v in arms.items()}
assert 'control' in arms, 'need control=...'
rows = []
for arm, runs in arms.items():
    for s, run in enumerate(runs):
        for d in ('b10', 'b01'):
            f = f'{W}/runs/{run}_{d}/eval_preds.npz'
            if not os.path.exists(f): print('MISSING', f); continue
            z = np.load(f); P, G = z['P'], z['G']
            for j in c11:
                m = M[G, j]; rows.append(dict(arm=arm, seed=s, run=run, direction=d, target=names[j], r=float(np.corrcoef(P[m, j], Y[G[m], j])[0, 1])))
df = pd.DataFrame(rows); df.to_csv(os.path.join(out, 'goal_arms.csv'), index=False)
g = df.groupby(['arm', 'seed', 'direction']).r.mean().unstack('direction'); g['GOAL'] = g.mean(axis=1); g = g.reset_index()
ok = g.dropna(subset=['GOAL'])
summ = ok.groupby('arm')[['b10', 'b01', 'GOAL']].mean(); summ['n_seeds'] = ok.groupby('arm').size()
c = ok[ok.arm == 'control'].set_index('seed').GOAL
summ['delta_vs_control_paired'] = [float((ok[ok.arm == a].set_index('seed').GOAL - c).dropna().mean()) for a in summ.index]
summ = summ.round(4); summ.to_csv(os.path.join(out, 'goal_summary.csv')); print(summ.to_string())
pt = df.groupby(['arm', 'target']).r.mean().unstack('arm'); print(pt.round(3).to_string())
ok.rename(columns={'GOAL': 'value'})[['arm', 'value', 'seed']].to_csv(os.path.join(out, 'plot_goal.csv'), index=False)

item.aggregated_output:
Rotating a crop would change which physical illumination direction a channel describes, so the record recipe uses translations.
[Architecture caption](figures/overview/CAPTIONS.md) · [Teacher code](scripts/train_lf.py) · [View construction](bsccm/ssl.py)

### Start with the saved predictions

On the project cluster the packed data, weights and saved predictions already have the paths expected by the scripts.
The following Bash commands run from the repository root. They need NumPy and pandas and write only into a fresh output directory.
Use any Python 3 environment with NumPy and pandas on the CPU. The training commands use Apptainer.

```bash
# From the repository root, score the archived predictions in a subshell.
(
set -eu
repo=$PWD
W=/hnvme/workspace/v181bb10-bsccm
out=$(mktemp -d)
require_predictions() {
  if [[ ! -s "$1" ]]; then
    printf 'Missing predictions: %s\n' "$1" >&2
    return 1
  fi
}

# Check all positions in the two directions before calculating a mean.
for member in n048_v9_base n048_v9_zoom2 n053_cytoland n053_cytoland_s1 n051_v10_base; do
  for d in b10 b01; do
    require_predictions "$W/runs/${member}_${d}/eval_preds.npz"
  done
done
for member in n083_cnxs60_s1_b10 n084_cnxs120_s1_b01; do
  require_predictions "$W/runs/$member/eval_preds.npz"
done

# Single models. Each arm names a run prefix without its _b10 or _b01 suffix.
python3 -I scripts/score_goal_arms.py "$out" \
  control=n048_v9_base zoom=n048_v9_zoom2 cytoland=n053_cytoland

# N053 averages saved predictions row by row, then scores the common 11.
python3 -I .agent-research/results/N053-*/n053_score.py "$out/n053.csv" \
  n048_v9_base+n048_v9_zoom2+n053_cytoland \
  n048_v9_base+n048_v9_zoom2+n053_cytoland_s1

# N084 uses different ConvNeXt-S run names for the two directions.
# Its scorer writes n084_scores.csv in the current directory.
(cd "$out" && python3 -I "$repo"/.agent-research/results/N084-*/n084_score.py)
printf 'Scores: %s\n' "$out"
)
```

`eval_preds.npz` contains a prediction matrix `P` and global cell-row IDs `G`.
The N053 scorer verifies the same row order across members. Every scorer above reads **v10** measurements for those IDs.
In `score_goal_arms.py`, comma-separated runs are replicate **seeds**. It writes `goal_arms.csv` (target-level), `goal_summary.csv` and `plot_goal.csv`.
Use the N053 scorer's **plus-separated** syntax for an ensemble. The fine-tuner's generic validation mean can include a different set of columns. [Arm scorer](scripts/score_goal_arms.py) · [N053 scorer](.agent-research/results/N053-lf-encoder-swap-on-the-v10-goal-dinov3-v/n053_score.py) · [N084 scorer](.agent-research/results/N084-pre-registered-ensemble-confirmation-n05/n084_score.py)

| Expected check on saved predictions | Draw 1 → 0 | Draw 0 → 1 | GOAL | MM3 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| N053, three members | .7001 | .6723 | .6862 | .7734 |
| N053, retrain only Cytoland with seed 1 | .7043 | .6685 | .6864 | — |
| N084, add ConvNeXt-S to seed-0 N053 | .7030 | .6793 | .6911 | .7764 |

These numbers can be reproduced from the archived predictions without retraining. The two ResNet *training* label files differ from the *scoring* file.
Replacing the cofactor-150 ResNets with the v10-trained controls changes the ensemble. [N048 jobs](.agent-research/results/N048-label-v9-asinh-cofactor-from-a-pre-regis/jobs.txt) · [N053 seed replication](.agent-research/results/N053-lf-encoder-swap-on-the-v10-goal-dinov3-v/n053_followup.csv) · [N084 score table](.agent-research/results/N084-pre-registered-ensemble-confirmation-n05/n084_scores.csv)

### Rebuild the members on the cluster

**1. Prepare the inputs.** The necessary files are listed in [Repository and cluster](#repository-and-cluster).
For a rebuild from raw data, N001 records fetching and verifying the Dryad chunks, making the indexed zip and packing the arrays.
N005 adds the LF flat fields, slide scales and target masks. N029 excludes Giemsa cells from calibration and N036 cross-fits the spatial detrend.
The N048 and N051 build scripts call the versioned target builders with the cofactor and cross-fit settings needed for the final label files.
The Cytoland adapter expects the converted VSCyto2D weights at the path in `bsccm/cytoland.py`.
[N001 packing][N001] · [LF calibration][N005] · [cf150 build](.agent-research/results/N048-label-v9-asinh-cofactor-from-a-pre-regis/n048_build.sh) · [v10 build](.agent-research/results/N051-label-v10-per-marker-asinh-cofactor-pre/n051_build2.sh) · [Cytoland loader](bsccm/cytoland.py)

**2. Locate or recreate the source-draw SSL checkpoints.** N031's `jobs.txt` records the job IDs only. These are equivalent trainer invocations reconstructed from its item and the trainer defaults. Their settings agree with the archived offline run configurations.
Run the following Bash blocks in order from the repository root in the same GPU allocation. Each direction needs the completed `encoder_final.pt` from its own source draw. The two directions can use separate GPUs. The commands below run each trainer directly with Apptainer on an allocated GPU.

On the original cluster, `scripts/gpu_job.sbatch` submits one trainer per SLURM job. It hard-codes the checkout at `$HOME/BSCCM` and the cluster log directory, and calls `~/.claude/skills/work-log/bin/preempt-run.sh`, a helper outside this repository. The plain `apptainer exec` command below runs with the built image and the packed workspace mounted at the paths expected by the trainers. [N031 recipe][N031] · [SSL trainer](scripts/train_ssl_lf.py) · [GPU wrapper](scripts/gpu_job.sbatch)

```bash
W=/hnvme/workspace/v181bb10-bsccm
# Create a NEW directory under runs/ for this rebuild and keep its name for every step.
build=$(mktemp -d "$W/runs/rebuild_XXXXXXXX")
printf 'Rebuild directory: %s\n' "$build"
ssl_root=$build
gpu() {
  [[ -d "${build:?Set up the rebuild directory first}" ]] || return 1
  WANDB_MODE=offline apptainer exec --nv --bind "$W" "$W/env/bsccm.sif" python3 -I "$@"
}

# Each SSL checkpoint goes in a NEW subdirectory of "$build".
for heldout in 0 1; do
  gpu scripts/train_ssl_lf.py --arm aug --out "$build/n031_ssl_aug_ex$heldout" --arch resnet50 --epochs 40 --bs 512 --views 2 --lr 0.002 --lam 0.05 --proj-dim 256 --rows all --exclude-batch "$heldout" --seed 0
done

# BSCCM · Predicting white blood cell markers from label-free images

Can a microscope image tell us how much of a protein a white blood cell carries, even in a fresh blood sample?
We train an image encoder to predict fluorescence-derived marker levels and use it as a teacher for a second model that reads stained blood smears.
Our primary score, **GOAL**, averages prediction–measurement correlations for 11 targets when we train on one blood draw and test on the other.
Through N090 (24 November 2026), the target is **.700**. The official record is **.6862** (N053, three members). Cytoland was selected after testing four candidates on the evaluation draws. Retraining that member alone gave .6864.
The strongest primary ensemble result so far was **.6911** (N084, four members) against an improvement threshold of **.6916**.
Bright markers associated with cell type transfer well. Dim markers depend strongly on how fluorescence background is estimated.
Across three ImageStream donors, training on one marker per cell weakened predicted CD4–CD8 exclusivity. The differences between training regimes were statistically inconclusive.
On MLL23, a reused clinical development benchmark, the Giemsa student learned better class rankings from LF features than from marker outputs. The AUROC gain of .113 passed the registered .074 effect-size rule, but the paired test across three teachers gave p = .07. [GOAL register](.agent-research/notebook/GOAL.md) · [Overview figures](figures/overview/CAPTIONS.md)

**Reading guide** · [Data and terminology](#what-one-training-example-contains) · [Data and checkpoints](#data-and-checkpoints) · [Evaluation](#what-counts-as-progress) · [Results by task](#what-worked-for-each-task) · [Reproduction](#reproduce-the-marker-ensembles) · [Repository and cluster](#repository-and-cluster) · [Experiment history](#experiment-history) · [Figures](#figure-gallery) · [Current work](#current-work-and-open-questions)

## What one training example contains

**BSCCM** stands for Berkeley Single Cell Computational Microscopy. It contains **412,941 human white blood cells**.
An LED array illuminates each cell in several ways while a camera records the same crop.
Brightfield shows transmitted light. Darkfield emphasizes light scattered by the cell.

```
